questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in a big city in the US for my exchange and so Boston was a perfect choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is super easy. The university and Sage are very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a week long orientation full of information and activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You choose 3 options I think but most exchange students got put in the hotel.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is no kitchen and there is a mandatory meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The hotel is a great option. Be happy if you get it since living with all the other students there is a lot of fun. I think there were more than a 100 of us and making friends is very easy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up very early in April which is good for the approval at KU

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always email the coordinator or professors to get off waitlists etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The original classes I wanted were not available but from the ones I saw on the final list, I got all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The worst part was that many of the courses that are shown for Fall/Spring semester do not get taught every year and so not all are actually an option. Hence, many courses I initially wanted to do were unavailable. So prepare many possible courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is lower than KU, like the speed of lectures is slower and there is more time to understand new concepts with many lecturers giving extensive recaps every lecture.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are more assignments which count for small portions of your grade. This makes the exams less important

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CASMA 568 - Statistical Analysis of Point Process Data, CASMA 578 - Numerical Methods for Biological Sciences, AS 105 - Alien Worlds

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to pick something outside of your major, pick Alien Worlds. it is really interesting and JJ Hermes is a great professor. The course is an intro to astronomy for non-astronomy students and so he keeps it very fun. It is a general education requirement for many people at BU so you are surrounded by many 3 or 4th year students who are in other majors and it is a nice mix.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Honestly, once you have the meal plan, your day to day spending can become 0 for a lot of the days.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out and traveling (especially during thanksgiving). Generally, prices are similar to Copenhagen though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs. Like everything from acapella to dance to cultural clubs to board games or even the ski club. I joined the outing club, chess club, marine science and many more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the outing club!!! A great way to see some places in New Hampshire and Maine and to just see the countryside of New England. The people are so fun and it is a great way to meet people outside the exchange student bubble.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: NYC, DC, Chicago, Acadia National Park (with the outing club!!!!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy as Americans are super friendly and open compared to Danish people. Sometimes, it can seem fake to us but they are really good at remembering you and always saying hi to you and making small talk.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just engage in small talk, join clubs and go to all the orientation events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some Americans are uncomfortable with silence and so it can be challenging when they say stuff just to say stuff. This is not something I will ever get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way people you havent seen since orientation still say hi to you and engage in conversations. People are a lot more approachable for small interactions and do not take themselves that seriously.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get the on campus housing to be in the middle of social life, say yes to all travel plans and plans that people make in the beginning and try to open your perspective a little. Just because Americans (or other cultures) do things differently, does not make it any better or worse. Many European exchange students come here and sometimes look down on American culture, which I think is not the best attitude to have.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not expect a crazy nightlife. It is very tame compared to many European cities and most places are super expensive and close around 1 am.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I have made and travels I have done with these new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The current political situation is very unstable and so the visa situation was a big mess. It is not a great start to always have doubts that your exchange might not happen. In hindsight, I probably would have rather applied to Canada or Australia to still get a different Anglophone culture and not have doubts about whether my exchange would happen. However, once you are here, it is an amazing time!!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
